reason: Both meet all hard constraints (heading order, snapshot-before-risk, no restart/failover before snapshot, explicit abort condition), but Response B is more operationally concrete: it adds a snapshot-failure escalation path (relevant given the disk is nearly full), a numeric abort trigger (10-minute latency check) with guidance against stacking mitigations, and quantified resolution criteria in FOLLOW UP (e.g., disk below 80%, latency within 1.2x baseline for 30 minutes), making it more directly actionable as a real runbook.
